correction.text: the Cotabato Valley, 'largely centered around the Cotabato Valley': Maguindanao, Cotabato and Sultan Kudarat provinces

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1515-1520: established in 1515 by Sharif Kabungsuwan (infobox), Cliopatria starts in 1521. The page 'ruled parts of the island of Mindanao' and was 'largely centered around the Cotabato Valley'. It gives no area.

correction.text: the Cotabato Valley, 'largely centered around the Cotabato Valley': Maguindanao, Cotabato and Sultan Kudarat provinces

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 106,474 km2 (332 cells over Bukidnon, Agusan del Sur, Zamboanga, Davao, Surigao: all of central and eastern Mindanao) lies cell for cell inside its Sultanate of Brunei 1521 shape, which is a Brunei overlay, not the Maguindanao state. The page puts the sultanate 'largely' in the Cotabato Valley, with influence 'from the peninsula of Zamboanga to bay of Sarangani until Davao Gulf'; the influence is not control. Use the valley. About 14,000 km2 by the three provinces. Applies 1521-1624; the Sarangani islands are added in 1625.

correction.text: the Cotabato Valley plus the Sarangani islands captured in 1625

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1612-1848 shape is a single cell (372 km2) in Davao del Norte, 150 km from the Maguindanao heartland, while its Spanish Empire shape (and from 1880 the Kingdom of Spain) covers the Cotabato valley from the 1600s. The sultanate lasted, an independent state under Kudarat and his successors, to 1899. Use the valley and the Sarangani islands, which 'Subjugated since its capture in 1625'. Applies 1625-1861.

correction.text: the Cotabato Valley plus the Sarangani islands, unchanged to 1861

keyframe_review.note: Same one-cell shape, 1849-1852, and the same error: Maguindanao did not end in 1852; its sultans signed friendly treaties with Spain in 1837 and 1845 and had a Spanish flag hoisted at Polloc under duress only in 1862 ('a small fleet forced the Sultan of Mindanao to hoist a Spanish flag at Polloc'). The shape holds until the 1862 loss of Polloc; the later years are the 1862 keyframe.

correction.text: the Cotabato Valley and the Sarangani islands without the Spanish enclave at Polloc

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1862-1899, a period Cliopatria lacks: after 1862 the valley minus Polloc, the Parang coast where 'a small fleet forced the Sultan of Mindanao to hoist a Spanish flag'. The Spanish took forts on the Rio Grande in 1864 and Tumbao on 1 January 1887, but the sultanate (Cotabato 1861-1888, Libungan 1896-1900) held the valley until the American occupation of December 1899.

region.text: the Cotabato Valley, 'largely centered around the Cotabato Valley': Maguindanao, Cotabato and Sultan Kudarat provinces

ledger.note: 1515: Sharif Kabungsuwan founds the Sultanate of Maguindanao. Infobox: established 1515 by Sharif Kabungsuwan, capital Tubok 1515-1543; the page gives the Cotabato Valley as the centre, not a boundary.
1543: the capital moves from Tubok to Selangan (infobox 'Selangan (1543-1619; 1701-1711)').
1619: Sultan Kudarat takes the throne and the capital moves to Ramitan (infobox 'Ramitan (1619-1637)').

region.text: Buayan, which 'would become a de facto subject state under Sultan Kudarat'

ledger.note: 1619: Buayan becomes a de facto subject of Kudarat. The page says Maguindanao had a rivalry with Buayan, which 'would become a de facto subject state under Sultan Kudarat' (reign 1619-1671) and that Kudarat unified the 'sa ilud and sa raya polities'; it gives neither a year nor a boundary. The date is Kudarat's accession and the region is my reading; Spain and Buayan had agreed in 1605 'to recognize Rajah Silongan as the paramount ruler of Maguindanao' (Spanish-Moro conflict page).

region.text: the Sarangani islands, 'Subjugated since its capture in 1625'

ledger.note: 1625: Maguindanao captures the Sarangani islands. 'Capture of the Sarangani islands' in 1625, 'Subjugated since its capture in 1625'. Kudarat also consolidated tribute from Iranun, Maranao, Manobo and Tiruray peoples and from Davao 'by force', undated.
1639: the capital moves to Simuay, Kudarat's free trading port (infobox 'Simuay (1639-1701)').
1671: Kudarat dies and Buayan's subjection lapses. Page silent: the date is the end of Kudarat's reign (1619-1671); the page does not say when or how the subjection ended.
1711: the capital moves to Tamontaka, where it stays until 1861 (infobox 'Tamontaka (1711-1861)').

region.text: Polloc, on the Parang coast: 'a small fleet forced the Sultan of Mindanao to hoist a Spanish flag at Polloc'

ledger.note: 1862: Spain plants its flag at Polloc. 'At the same time a small fleet forced the Sultan of Mindanao to hoist a Spanish flag at Polloc' (dated 1862); the Spanish then expanded from Polloc up the Rio Grande ('In September 1864 an expedition was sent from Polloc against the Rio Grande Moros' and took the fort at Pagalungan).

region.text: the Cotabato Valley, 'American occupation of Cotabato'

ledger.note: 1899: American troops occupy Cotabato. The page: 'December 1899: American occupation of Cotabato'; in December 1900 Mangigin moved to Sibugay; the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1899 or 1926' (Mangigin died in 1926) and Insular Government of the Philippines and Moro Province as successors. Spain had held the valley only by a flag at Polloc and forts on the Rio Grande (1887, Tumbao).

wars.name: Spanish and Maguindanao campaign against Rajah Silongan
wars.outcome: 'In April 1596, Rajah Silongan held off against the joint forces of Maguindanao and Spain.' In 1605 Spain and Buayan agreed to recognise Silongan as the paramount ruler of Maguindanao.
wars.note: The page does not mention Figueroa's expedition. No land is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Kudarat and Corralat's wars with Spain
wars.outcome: Spain built the Real Fuerza de San Jose at Zamboanga in 1635; the Spanish made peace with Corralat in 1642 (the Maguindanao page has a 1645 peace treaty with the Zamboanga governor), burned his town in 1656 and evacuated Zamboanga in January 1663; they returned in 1718.
wars.note: No Maguindanao land is recorded as changing hands. Lanao drove the Spanish out about 1640 and 'seceded from the Maguindanao sultanate' in the 17th century (Maguindanao page, undated).

wars.name: Spanish expeditions from Polloc
wars.outcome: Polloc taken in 1862; the fort at Pagalungan captured after the expedition of September 1864; Tumbao occupied on 1 January 1887 by Lieutenant-Colonel Matos, with Datu Uto returning on 10 March with peace conditions. The valley otherwise stayed with the sultan.
wars.note: No end of the Spanish occupation of these forts is dated on the page. The circle for the Rio Grande is a guess.

wars.name: American occupation of Cotabato
wars.outcome: 'American occupation of Cotabato', December 1899; the sultan Mangigin moved to Sibugay in December 1900.
wars.note: The Spanish-Moro page does not discuss the American takeover.

certainty.note: The sultanate was a river-valley state with tribute zones round it; no survey or treaty line. Polloc (1862) is the only point with a dated Spanish claim.

notes:
Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Neither gives an area, so the Cliopatria area could not be compared.
CLIOPATRIA ERRORS: the 1521-1608 shape is the Sultanate of Brunei's Mindanao shape (332 of 332 cells inside Brunei 1521), not the Maguindanao sultanate; the 1612-1848 and 1849-1852 shape is a single cell at Davao; the row ends in 1852 although the sultanate lasted to 1899. Cliopatria's Spanish Empire (and from 1880 Kingdom of Spain) shape covers the Cotabato valley from the 1600s, which these pages do not support: the Spanish held Zamboanga 1635-1663 and from 1718, Polloc from 1862 and Tumbao in 1887. The Brunei dossier (se-02) must be told that its Mindanao interior is not documented here.
PAGE SILENT: Buayan's status and region (a vassal pair at confidence 1); Davao's Kalagan tribute; the Iranun/Maranao/Manobo/Tiruray tribute zones; when Lanao seceded; the garbled 1705 'ceded the island of Palawan to the Spanish government'; the 1645 peace (the Spanish-Moro page has 1642); the Spanish founding of Cotabato; the extent of Maguindanao in 1515; the capitals' sites.
NEEDS DOSSIERS: Buayan Sultanate (rival, then subject of Kudarat), Lanao (Maranao confederacies). The United States (1900 shape) holds the valley in Cliopatria.
Gazetteer: Tubok, Selangan, Ramitan, Simuay, Tamontaka, Libungan, Polloc, Tumbao, Pagalungan and the Sarangani islands are not in the gazetteer; the Sarangani islands (Balut) lie in Davao Occidental, which the admin1 table lacks.
